title: Tencent Loses Access to 100,000 AI Chips After Oracle Scraps $7B Agreement
summary:
The software provider Oracle has called off a long-term agreement to provide high-end cloud infrastructure to the Chinese company Tencent, a move that will strip the tech giant of a planned source of processing power for its AI models. The agreement, valued at approximately $7B, would have granted Tencent access to 100,000 advanced AI chips across Southeast Asian data centers over five years to circumvent trade restrictions currently in place within China. The partnership effectively ceased before the U.S. midterm elections after the Trump administration approached Oracle with security concerns regarding the lease.

The collapse of the deal comes as senior Guangdong officials urged Tencent to prioritize domestic chipmakers and as Nvidia issued guidelines requiring cloud providers to sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies. This loss of planned compute capacity arrives as Tencent's Hunyuan AI models were closing the performance gap with Alibaba's Qwen. Neither Oracle, Tencent, nor the White House have issued public comments on the reported cancellation.

selectedTweets.text:
Oracle $ORCL has reportedly canceled a $7B AI chip leasing deal with Tencent following pressure from the Trump administration, according to the FT.

The five-year agreement would have given Tencent access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips across Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia, making it Tencent's largest overseas chip leasing deal.

The arrangement would have allowed Tencent to use advanced computing hardware unavailable inside China because of U.S. and Chinese restrictions.

U.S. officials reportedly approached Oracle with concerns about the agreement. Meanwhile, senior Chinese officials visited Tencent and urged the company to support domestic chipmakers.

Although overseas AI chip leasing remains permitted under existing rules, the deal has now been canceled following pressure from both Washington and Beijing.

Oracle, Tencent, and the White House have not publicly commented on the reported cancellation.

selectedTweets.text:
Oracle has scrapped a $7B lease giving Tencent up to 100K advanced AI chips after US objections.

The 5-year contract, Tencent’s largest overseas lease, would have supplied chips unavailable in China from data centres across south-east Asia.

Chinese labs rent that capacity mainly for model training, which domestic chips can’t yet handle.

China pushed from the other side, as senior Guangdong officials visited Tencent and urged it to back domestic chips, one person said.

Such leases remain legal, but Nvidia has now told cloud clients to sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies.

Tighter export controls had already pushed these leases toward higher prices, longer terms and bigger upfront payments, so every cancellation strips premium revenue from US cloud providers.

With both governments squeezing that route, Tencent loses planned compute just as its Hunyuan models were closing the gap with Alibaba’s Qwen.
